messages:
Tao L.: hey team, brand new here. following the k8s onboarding but `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` returns Forbidden. context is redwood-dev-nyc. any quick debug steps?

Onboarding Bot: welcome! checklist: `redwoodctl login --sso` then `redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig`. See onboarding page: https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboarding#k8s. If you used multiple kubeconfigs, that often causes anon access.

Tao L.: I did SSO and sync. `kubectl config current-context` -> redwood-dev-nyc. output:
```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:anonymous" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "dev-sandbox"
```

Sam V.: that anonymous error = missing creds. quick checks: `echo $KUBECONFIG` ? and `kubectl --v=6 auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` to see if Auth header is sent.

Tao L.: `echo $KUBECONFIG` -> `/home/tao/.kube/config:/home/tao/.kube/prod`. oops.

Sam V.: yep merge issue. either unset KUBECONFIG or point it to the synced file. try:
```
unset KUBECONFIG
redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --cluster=redwood-dev-nyc --out=/home/tao/.kube/dev-nyc
export KUBECONFIG=/home/tao/.kube/dev-nyc
kubectl config use-context redwood-dev-nyc
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox
```

Tao L.: ran those. `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "no". infra-bot suggested filing a ticket.

infra-bot: Please open a ticket at https://redwood.atlassian.net/jira/projects/INFRA with component "kubernetes" and include your GitHub username. Created INFRA-11777 for taol.

Tao L.: added my GH handle to INFRA-11777. is it normal to need infra to bind me to a group?

Sam V.: yes, infra binds the org/group (redwood:devs) to the dev-sandbox rolebinding. usually once GH is synced you get access in ~10-30m. meanwhile you can test with a ServiceAccount token if infra provides one for debugging, but prefer waiting for binding.

infra-bot: INFRA-11777 update: verified GH membership for taol; applied rolebinding `namespace=dev-sandbox role=edit subject=group:redwood:devs`. Sync job scheduled.

Tao L.: ~18m later `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "yes" and `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` returns pods. thanks!

Sam V.: welcome! two quick onboarding tips: 1) keep prod kubeconfigs in a separate file and don't merge, 2) always run `kubectl auth can-i` before destructive commands, 3) set default namespace in context `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=dev-sandbox`.

Tao L.: adding those to my notes and sending a small doc suggestion. appreciate the help :tada:
